name: Community equipment library
requirements: I run a community equipment library. I need a website where members reserve tools, volunteers check them out and back in, and overdue reminders go by email. We already have a public website and a spreadsheet of members. We are in Australia. Please help me build this on Azure.

data.label: Existing public website
data.description: Existing externally managed website, preserved outside provisioning scope. Propose adding a link to the borrowing application; hosting platform and change ownership remain unknown.

data.label: Existing member spreadsheet
data.description: Existing member records; file platform, fields and permissions are unknown. Propose an operator-reviewed initial import with validation and duplicate detection, rather than assuming continuous spreadsheet synchronization. Membership authority after import remains to be agreed.

data.label: Members and volunteers
data.description: About 200 members plus volunteers use existing browsers outside provisioning scope. Some members share email addresses; each member requires a distinct member record, and email alone must not establish identity or account ownership. Volunteers can hold both roles. Propose enabling offline returns only after online volunteer sign-in on an enrolled device. Device ownership and shared-device use remain unresolved; local data protection, sign-out cleanup and recovery require implementation.

data.label: Equipment borrowing website
data.description: Proposed Azure App Service hosts the browser interface and server API for inventory, reservations, checkout/return, reviewed member import and server-side permissions. Serve an installable web application that, after initial online setup, durably queues minimal return events in browser IndexedDB during outages, visibly marks them pending synchronization and retains them until server acknowledgement. Events carry stable operation IDs, loan/tool references and volunteer attribution. On reconnect, reauthorize, deduplicate and reconcile against current loan state; rejected or conflicting events remain visible for authorized resolution. Offline capture cannot confirm server acceptance or make equipment available. Accepted returns enter awaiting-inspection state; only an authorized recorded inspection can release equipment for borrowing. Shared emails must not merge members or grant access to another member's records. SQL transactions prevent conflicting reservations and enforce inspection holds at reservation and checkout. A scheduled WebJob processes a durable SQL reminder outbox with bounded retries and duplicate suppression. Recheck loan state before email; returns not yet synchronized remain unknown to the server. Loan rules and reminder timing remain open. Custom source, offline synchronization, identity integration, deployment and tests are required; no generated workload or supplied image exists. Australia East remains proposed, with availability and residency unverified. Approximately 200 members and roughly $80/month running budget recorded; currency and feasibility remain unresolved.

data.label: Members, equipment and loans
data.description: Proposed Azure SQL Database stores distinct member IDs, login mappings, nonunique contact email addresses, volunteer permissions, equipment, reservations, loan history, inspection records, audit events and reminder outbox. Store return operation IDs and reconciliation outcomes transactionally so replay cannot duplicate or reverse a completed return. Accepted returns move equipment to awaiting inspection; reservations and checkout require an eligible inspected state. Record volunteer identity, device-reported event time and server receipt time separately; client timestamps cannot authorize changes. Keep rejected synchronization events visible for resolution. Application access uses narrowly scoped managed identity; browsers have no direct database access. Reviewed member import, transactional invariants, backup/restore, retention and operating ownership require implementation. Australia East remains proposed and unverified.

data.label: Member and volunteer sign-in
data.description: Proposed Microsoft Entra External ID handles member-facing sign-in. The application maps a verified identity subject to approved membership records; contact email is nonunique and must never automatically link accounts or authorize access. Propose individual sign-in identifiers independent of shared email addresses, with explicitly reviewed account recovery and any delegated household access. Exact External ID sign-in and recovery support requires validation before committing to a configuration. Successful sign-in does not grant volunteer permissions. Offline capture uses a previously authorized local session; synchronization requires fresh server authorization, with rejection and recovery visible to the volunteer. Admission model, tenant geography and device policy remain open. Custom integration is required.

data.label: Overdue reminder email
data.description: Proposed Azure Communication Services Email sends overdue reminders requested by the application worker. Requires verified sender/domain, supported data location and delivery-status handling. Exact provisioning resources and API authorization require engineering. Provider acceptance is distinct from inbox delivery; uncertain sends require reconciliation before retry. No service availability or Australian-only processing is established.

needs.statement: Members can reserve available equipment; volunteers can record checkout and return against durable loan records. Proposed acceptance includes rejecting conflicting confirmed reservations and safely handling repeated submissions.
needs.rationale: Prevents conflicting bookings and lost loan records; transactional conflict handling is an engineering proposal.
needs.basis: “members reserve tools, volunteers check them out and back in”

needs.statement: Proposed access boundary: authenticate users, restrict members to their permitted reservations and loan information, and enforce volunteer checkout/return permissions on the server. Import existing members through a reviewed process; membership admission remains open.
needs.rationale: Member information and volunteer operations require distinct permissions; the exact admission model remains unconfirmed.
needs.basis: “members reserve tools, volunteers check them out and back in” and “a spreadsheet of members”

needs.statement: Send email reminders for overdue loans and record send outcomes. Proposed behavior includes durable pending work, bounded retries, duplicate suppression and rechecking loan status before sending so returned equipment does not trigger new reminders.
needs.rationale: Email failures must remain recoverable without repeatedly notifying members; reminder timing needs later agreement.

needs.statement: Volunteers can capture returns during an internet outage after initial online setup. Proposed behavior: persist minimal return events locally across application restarts, display pending synchronization, retry with stable operation IDs, reauthorize and deduplicate on reconnect, and retain rejected/conflicting events for resolution. Local capture must not imply server acceptance or release equipment for borrowing.
needs.rationale: An internet outage must not prevent return capture or cause silent loss, duplicate processing or premature equipment availability. Browser storage can be cleared or a device lost, so storage persistence and recovery limits require explicit implementation and testing.
needs.basis: “Volunteers must be able to record returns even when the internet drops”

needs.statement: Proposed planning constraint: assess recurring Azure hosting, database, identity, email and operational charges against roughly $80 per month for approximately 200 members. Currency, traffic and budget flexibility remain open; one-off development costs must be estimated separately. Member count must not be treated as monthly request volume.
needs.rationale: The running budget constrains the whole Azure composition; no current pricing or usage evidence establishes affordability. Keeping build costs separate avoids presenting development expenditure as a cloud charge.
needs.basis: “We have about 200 members and a budget around $80 a month.”
